verdict.rationale: Stripe's own docs claim verification of government-issued ID documents from more than 120 countries, which shows real documented breadth. A hands-on user also notes you can specify the accepted document types. However, the evidence never enumerates the document types (passports, national IDs, driver licenses, residence permits) or points to a published supported-country/document list, and community reports cite gaps such as unsupported Polish IDs and rejected Chinese passports. missing for 10: published per-country supported-document list, explicit enumeration of passports/national IDs/driver licenses/residence permits, independent corroboration of consistent coverage across listed countries.

support.subject: As an ops lead, the platform verifies government IDs from a documented breadth of countries and document types — passports, national IDs, driver licenses, residence permits — with the supported list published

citations.quote: Verify the authenticity of government-issued ID documents from more than 120 countries
Capture government-issued photo IDs with a conversion-optimized verification flow
I like that it lets you specify the types of accepted docs.
